transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-05-06
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees (recorded): Jordan Hale (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood Solutions), Evelyn Park (NovaMed Head of ML), Carlos Mendez (CTO), Samir Gupta (Data Engineer), Leah Kim (Regulatory)

Summary: quick scoping for a 4-week POC to validate open-model shortlist for multilingual clinical note summarization and triage. Discussed success criteria (latency, throughput, quality measures), workload sizing (expected qps, document lengths), bench plan, and timeline. Agreed on 2-week bench sprint + 2-week integration/pilot. Action items and next steps captured.

Topics: POC goals; model shortlist and tradeoffs; benchmark metrics and configs; infra options (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC); security/compliance asks; timeline and deliverables.

Action items (read back): Priya to run bench configs; Samir to share sample data; Jordan to share docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. um we wanted to run through the POC playbook and make sure the scope's tight. Evelyn thanks for setting this up.
[00:10] Evelyn: yeah thanks, Jordan. quick intro from our side — i'm Evelyn, head of ML at NovaMed. we need a POC to test summarization + triage for outpatient clinical notes across en/es/pt. key constraints are PHI handling, latency for the triage endpoint and cost per thousand tokens.
[00:25] Carlos: and i just want to add the business timeline: clinical pilot in Q3, so we need a working POC in the next 6 weeks ideally.
[00:33] Priya: got it. real quick — do you have an initial success metric for summarization quality? ROUGE? F1 for triage?
[00:40] Evelyn: good question. for summarization we care about factuality and key-entity recall, roughly target 0.75 F1 on our label set. for triage (urgent / routine) we want >0.9 recall on urgent cases and latency under 300ms p95 for single-turn inference ideally.
[00:55] Samir: latency under 300ms p95 — ok that pushes us toward dedicated or optimized hosted configs. what's the expected throughput?
[01:02] Evelyn: peak is small — maybe 12 QPS for triage during clinic hours, average closer to 2 QPS. but nightly batch summarization will hit higher tokens. estimate 80k tokens/day normal, burst to 200k on heavy nights.
[01:18] Liam: thanks, that helps. so for the bench we'll need both low-latency single-request tests and throughput streaming tests. Priya — suggest we run a continuous batching profile and a single-request cold-cache profile.
[01:28] Priya: yep we will. quick note: sometimes the transcript generator mislabels things — we may say 'Redwood Dedicated' but the infra option is Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPUs) or Private (VPC). we should test at least one dedicated GPU config and one hosted optimized config with quantization.
[01:44] Carlos: okay, can you give us a recommended open-model shortlist? we prefer open models for data residency and fine-tuning possibilities.
[01:50] Jordan: for this workload i would propose a small shortlist: 1) Llama-3-16B-chat (quantized) — good on general reasoning and multilingual with adapters, 2) Mistral-22B-instruct — strong instruction following and cost/quality balance, 3) Glacier-30B (open 30B variant, we call it Glacier internally) — higher quality on long-form clinical text but more resource heavy, 4) MPT-7B-Instruct for a lighter baseline.
[02:15] Evelyn: curious — Mistral-22B vs Llama-3-16B, which wins on Spanish/Portuguese?
[02:20] Priya: in our internal evals Mistral tends to be better on generative quality in en/es, but Llama-3 exhibits stronger structured output and is easier to control with system prompts. there's a tradeoff: Mistral often has fewer hallucinations on narrative, Llama-3 is cheaper after quantization and lower latency.
[02:36] Samir: for clinical factuality, any preference? hallucination is our big risk.
[02:40] Priya: Glacier-30B is the safest for factuality given current weights, but it will require more GPU memory and possibly dedicated nodes. we can also try adapter tuning on Llama-3 to close the gap.
[02:52] Leah: from compliance — we need to ensure audit logs, KMS integration, and the ability to retain logs for 7 years. SOC2 is a minimum. can Redwood support per-tenant KMS and exportable audit trails?
[03:05] Jordan: yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS and long-term audit exports. for hosted we'll provide SOC2 docs; for heavy-regulated deployment we'd recommend Private with VPC peering or an on-prem bundle. i'll drop the security checklist.
[03:16] Evelyn: perfect. back to bench design — what's the bench timeline?
[03:20] Priya: propose two-week bench sprint: week 1 — model onboarding + microbench (latency, cold vs warm, token throughput), week 2 — quality evals (F1/rouge/entity recall) and cost estimates. following that a 2-week integration pilot where we wire infra, logging, fallback policies. total 4 weeks to a minimally viable POC.
[03:38] Carlos: can Redwood run benchmarks on our sample data or do we need to provide infra?
[03:42] Jordan: we can run initial benches in Redwood Hosted for speed, but to hit enterprise SLOs we'll run final benches on Dedicated or Private configurations — we'll need a representative dataset you supply for accurate cost numbers.
[03:53] Samir: we can share 500 anonymized notes and schema by Friday. note sizes vary, average 800 tokens, with about 5% >2k tokens.
[04:02] Priya: that distribution matters — we'll include seq_len 512, 1024, and 2048 runs. for tokenization variability across es/pt we'll ensure unicode test coverage.
[04:12] Evelyn: what about caching? can you leverage KV cache for multi-turn or long notes?
[04:17] Priya: yes, prefix caching and KV cache improves repeated-context latency. for single-shot triage caching less useful, but for summarization of large notes we can chunk and reuse caches. we'll measure both approaches.
[04:29] Carlos: and quantization — does Redwood support int8 or int4 flows?
[04:33] Priya: we support int8 and experimental int4 paths; i would default to int8 quantization for production-like benching to be conservative. int4 can get you cost down but sometimes degrades entity-level recall. we'll include a quantization sweep in the bench matrix.
[04:48] Jordan: cost targets? Evelyn mentioned tokens/day; any hard cap?
[04:51] Evelyn: we'd like to keep inference cost under $0.10 per 1k effective tokens for the POC. if dedicated nodes keep us under that we're happy.
[04:58] Priya: we'll produce per-model cost estimates: cost/token for hosted vs dedicated plus amortized storage. also include expected GPU hours for nightly batches.
[05:07] Samir: about evaluation — we want label-level metrics and a small human eval for factuality. can Redwood help run labelling for 200 samples?
[05:14] Liam: we don't do labeling, but we can integrate with your labeling vendor and provide the eval harness and dashboards; we can run automated metrics and produce a human-eval template you can use.
[05:24] Evelyn: okay, acceptable.
[05:27] Carlos: any fallback strategies if a chosen model has latency spikes?
[05:31] Priya: we support policy-based routing — route to cheaper model during low load, or fallback to a smaller model for degraded capacity. plus orange-level graceful degradation to cached responses. we'll define canary and fallback policies as part of the rollout plan.
[05:44] Evelyn: great. one more — data residency: some notes must stay within EU. we have a EU clinic. can we pin inference regionally?
[05:52] Jordan: yes, region pinning is supported. for Private/VPC you can ensure workloads run in EU-only infra. we'll capture this as a requirement.
[05:59] Samir: ok checklist for us: sample data, list of red flags for triage labels, cost constraint, and timeline. we'll aim to deliver samples by Friday.
[06:08] Jordan: perfect. i'll share the playbook: bench configs, SLO template, and a short security pack.
[06:13] Evelyn: how will we measure hallucinations specifically? entity hallucination?
[06:17] Priya: we'll run entity-level precision/recall against a curated gold set, plus a factuality spot-check using human raters. we'll include an inject test set with known contradictions to see model calibration.
[06:27] Carlos: for the bench, what hardware are you planning?
[06:30] Priya: host bench will run on our newest Ampere reserved instances; Dedicated will run on A100-80GB for the larger models. for the 16B/22B families we'll try 80GB or multi-GPU sharded runs depending on memory.
[06:44] Samir: is multi-GPU sharding supported for KV cache? we saw artifacts with some runtimes earlier.
[06:49] Priya: yes we support sharded KV cache and streaming across GPUs; there can be throughput tradeoffs but we mitigate with optimized kernel selection. we'll capture perf numbers.
[06:59] [Speaker 1]: (inaudible question about pricing tiers)
[07:02] Jordan: pricing will be usage-based for hosted, reserved commits for Dedicated. we'll provide a small pilot pricing worksheet.
[07:08] Evelyn: okay let's recap the success criteria — i'll read back to ensure shared understanding: 1) summarization quality: entity recall >= 0.75 F1; 2) triage recall for urgent >= 0.9; 3) triage p95 latency <= 300ms on single-turn; 4) cost <= $0.10 per 1k tokens; 5) audit logs and KMS in place. correct?
[07:26] Jordan: yes, that's correct. we'll add regional pinning for EU.
[07:31] Carlos: timeline recap?
[07:33] Priya: two-week bench sprint starting next Monday, with initial bench report at end of week 2, then two-week integration where we test Dedicated/Private and finalize pilot. total 4 weeks.
[07:44] Evelyn: and deliverables? bench report, security pack, cost estimates, eval dashboards.
[07:49] Jordan: correct. i'll attach the playbook and bench template after the call.
[07:53] Samir: quick operational ask, we need an engineer-level contact for bench infra that can ssh or coordinate networking for VPC tests.
[07:59] Jordan: noted — Liam will be the infra contact.
[08:03] Liam: happy to take that.
[08:06] Evelyn: any blockers from Redwood?
[08:08] Priya: none on our side; just need the sample data and the go-ahead for the bench window.
[08:13] Carlos: ok we'll send samples and red-flag list by Friday.
[08:18] Jordan: great, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench kickoff (1h) and share docs. thanks everyone.

End transcript.

References and links mentioned: playbook draft (link): https://redwood.example/poc-playbook (placeholder), security checklist: https://redwood.example/security-pack (placeholder).

Readout (final): agreed POC scope, shortlist of 4 open models to bench, bench matrix to include quantization sweep + seq_len variants, two-week bench + two-week integration, action items and next steps recorded above.
